prompt: An angle is drawn "in standard position." Which description is correct?

choices.label: The vertex is at the origin and the initial side lies along the positive $x$-axis.
The vertex is at the origin and the initial side lies along the positive $y$-axis.
The vertex can be anywhere, as long as the angle opens counterclockwise.
The vertex is at the origin and the terminal side lies along the positive $x$-axis.

hint: Standard position is a shared starting rule, so that everyone draws the same angle the same way.

hints.text: Standard position is a shared starting rule, so that everyone draws the same angle the same way.
Two things get pinned down: where the corner sits, and which ray you start from.
Corner at the origin, starting ray along the positive $x$-axis, then sweep counterclockwise for positive angles.

explanation: Standard position pins the vertex to the origin so every angle shares a corner.
It also pins the initial side — the ray you start from — along the positive $x$-axis.
The terminal side is wherever you stop after sweeping, so it is the one thing that is free to move.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why bother with a rule
steps: If everyone started their angles from a different ray, "$120^\circ$" would point somewhere different for each person.
Fixing the corner and the starting ray makes an angle measure into an address on the plane.
